sentences.text:
Applicant :- Sunny
Opposite Party :- State Of U.P.And 3 Others
Counsel for Applicant :- Shashi Kumar Mishra

Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Sameer Jain,J.
1. Sri Imran Khan, learned AGA for the State apprised the Court that on 26.07.2023 notice has been served upon the informant.
Despite service of notice, none appeared on behalf of the informant.

2. Heard Sri Anurag Dubey, Advocate holding brief of Sri S.K. Mishra, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri Imran Khan, learned AGA for the State.
3. The instant bail application has been filed seeking release of the applicant on bail in Case Crime No. 143 of 2023, under Sections 363, 376, 120B IPC and 3/4 POCSO Act, Police Station Jaithra,
District Etah during pendency of the trial.
4. FIR of the present case was lodged against applicant and one another and according to the FIR applicant has enticed away the minor daughter of the informant aged about 17 years.
5. Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that entire allegation made against the applicant is totally false and baseless and actually applicant and prosecutrix loved each other and prosecutrix,
Sunny vs State Of U.P.And 3 Others on 17 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/103553706/
1 who is major girl, had gone along with the applicant.
6.

entities.text: Sunny vs State Of U.P.And 3 Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He further submits that although applicant could not get the statements of the prosecutrix recorded under Sections 161 Cr.P.C. and 164 Cr.P.C. but to the best of his knowledge in both the statements prosecutrix did not make any allegation against the applicant.

He further submits that applicant is not having any criminal history and in the present matter he is in jail since 03.06.2023.
7.

Per contra, learned AGA opposed the prayer for bail and submits that there is allegation of enticement and rape against the applicant and as per school record, prosecutrix was around 17 years and 10 months old but he fairly conceded that as per statement recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C.
prosecutrix according to her own wish had gone along with applicant but when her statement under Section 164 Cr.P.C. was recorded then she even did not disclose the name of applicant and stated that she did not know him.
8. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.

9. Although, along with instant bail application the statements of the prosecutrix recorded under Sections 161 Cr.P.C. and 164 Cr.P.C. have not been appended but the same were produced by learned AGA during the course of argument and from the perusal of the statement of the prosecutrix recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C it appears that she according to her own wish had gone along with applicant but when her statement under Section 164 Cr.P.C. was recorded then she stated nothing against the applicant and stated that she did not even know him, therefore, it appears that there are material contradictions in her both the statements recorded under Sections 161 Cr.P.C. and 164 Cr.P.C.
10.

Therefore, considering the facts and circumstances of the case discussed above, in my view,
applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
11. Accordingly, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the instant bail application is allowed.

12. Let the applicant - Sunny be released on bail in the aforesaid case on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall appear before the trial court on the dates fixed, unless his personal presence is exempted.
(ii) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly, make inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
(iii) The applicant shall not indulge in any criminal and anti-social activity.
